name: Renaud
summary: Dual module bays, semi-permanent lunar surface base, potential Mars application. The vacuum-focused, deep-space-capable sibling of the LX-23.
description: LX-24 Renaud is the lunar long-stay base: dual module bays, a semi-permanent lunar surface base, with potential Mars application. Conceptually it is the vacuum-focused, deep-space-outfitted sibling of the LX-23 — the LX-23 has the propulsion legs (a fully-fuelled LX-23 is a “pseudo LX-24”) but lacks the long-duration life support and shielding the LX-24 is meant to carry. Roster-level entry plus this session’s thought experiment.

specs.note: Dual module bays, semi-permanent lunar base. Deep-space facilities (long-duration ECLSS, radiation shielding, crew provisions) are the point of difference vs LX-23. Not yet worked.

sections.heading: Relationship to the LX-23
sections.body: A fully-fuelled LX-23 has the propulsion to reach Mars orbit and even return (full-tank vacuum Δv ~7,780 m/s with 50 t), but lacks the 6–9 month transit life support and shielding. The LX-24 is the vehicle actually built for that — same airframe lineage, outfitted for the journey rather than improvised into it.

sections.heading: Roster note
sections.body: Dual bays, semi-permanent lunar base, potential Mars. Deep-space outfitting is the concept; no worked specs yet.

openItems: Full sizing pass — this vehicle exists only as a fleet-roster entry so far.
